seriesTitle: Rex Fleet Academy: Doctrine of Many Crowns
format: Topic-based Academy comic series; lecture/seminar framing with dramatized historical and operational case studies.
premise: Young Fleet personnel learn why the Five Crowns persist inside one Fleet. The series treats doctrine as a method for interrogating decisions, not a scoreboard for choosing a correct Crown.
coreProposition: No single truth of survival is sufficient to govern civilization.

Aurelian.failure: Preservation can become ossification, delay or rule by precedent.

Cerulean.truth: Coordination, beacons, command and shared situational awareness.
Cerulean.failure: Coordination can become centralization that treats local lives as parts of a system.

Ember.truth: Authority may need to act when consensus cannot.
Ember.failure: Emergency authority can perpetuate itself by finding another emergency.

Tempest.truth: Delay can be a decision and hesitation can kill.
Tempest.failure: Uncertainty can become justification for escalation.

Aegis.truth: Protection and convoy integrity are real duties.
Aegis.failure: Every shield creates a perimeter and somebody may remain outside it.

framingRules: Academy scenes must create dramatic questions; historical material is not a wiki lecture pasted into dialogue.
Historical reconstructions distinguish documented record, later testimony and Academy inference.
Crowns are institutional traditions, not personality types or five school houses.
No issue should designate a permanently correct Crown; show both what each lens sees and what it can miss.
Cadets may change positions. Do not map one recurring student permanently to one Crown.
Reach and Resolve is a common purpose above Crown rivalry, not a sixth and seventh Crown.
Living Memory may intersect later, but this series does not collapse doctrine into memorial ritual.
Released Rex Fleet canon outranks Academy reconstruction on any continuity conflict.
visualRules: Mature Fleet visual grammar is blue, gold and white.
Do not use full-field green as Aegis identity or full-field red as Ember identity; green and red retain their stronger regional/faction meanings elsewhere in current canon.
Differentiate Crown lineages primarily through crest geometry, material culture, ritual objects and restrained accents.
Historical Shattering-era scenes predate mature Fleet uniforms and formal Crown standardization.

issue1.title: Five Answers
issue1.spine: Professor Lysa Corven gives cadets five equivalent post-Shattering survival problems. Representative archive reconstructions dramatize the logic and failure mode later associated with Aurelian, Cerulean, Ember, Tempest and Aegis. The cadets expect one winning strategy; the reveal is that all five survived. The Doctrine of Many Crowns exists because no one survival truth is allowed to become civilization's permanent monopoly.

productionStatus: Initial RexPrompt production package. Issue 1 is scripted at page level and is a valid complete one-off. At most two follow-up issues may be developed if distinct source-backed problems justify them.

academyCurriculum.planStatus: Issue 1 is the default complete course; continuation is optional and capped at three total issues.
academyCurriculum.issueCountPolicy: Default 1; maximum expected 3. Do not create one issue per Crown.
academyCurriculum.sourceTextProgram: See academy_source_program.json. Oral histories, doctrine passages, orders, and later interpretations can form a documentary caption lane over reconstructions.

courseArchitecture.continuationRule: Issue 1 may stand alone. Any follow-up must combine genuinely distinct doctrine/historical problems; never create one issue per Crown by symmetry.
courseArchitecture.castScope: Professor Lysa Corven and the Issue 1 cohort are course-local unless explicitly reused.
courseArchitecture.imgScope: Use a dedicated Doctrine of Many Crowns IMG/reference project when visual production begins.
